analysis.investment_thesis: KPI Green Energy is a rare high-conviction growth story — 93% revenue CAGR and 82% net profit CAGR over six years in a sector with India's most powerful policy tailwind, yet trades at a modest P/E of just 20.6x. The dual IPP+CPP business model creates durable, contracted revenue streams that should compound for a decade as India races toward its 500 GW renewable target by 2030.
key_strengths: Exceptional revenue growth (92.6% CAGR) with expanding operating margins (30.58%), demonstrating pricing power uncommon in utilities
Secular tailwind: India's renewable energy transition is a multi-decade structural shift with government mandates, not cyclical demand
Attractive valuation — P/E of 20.6x and EV/EBITDA of 14.3x for a business compounding profits at 80%+ represents a significant margin of safety
key_risks: Persistently negative FCF (₹-1,297 Cr in FY25) and D/E of 0.88 signal capital addiction — growth is entirely debt/equity raise dependent, which Fisher finds structurally uncomfortable
Capex of ₹1,505 Cr in FY25 dwarfs operating cash flow of ₹208 Cr — execution risk is high if credit markets tighten or project IRRs compress
Utility-grade innovation moat — no proprietary technology or R&D differentiation; competitive advantage rests on execution speed and land/grid access, which are replicable
red_flags: FCF negative in all 5 years (-₹1,297 Cr in FY25); balance sheet tripled in one year to ₹6,164 Cr, financed almost entirely by ₹1,807 Cr financing CF
CWIP jumped to ₹709 Cr — large capital locked in under-construction projects creates execution and revenue recognition risk
DII ownership at 0.62% is very low — institutional conviction from domestic funds is conspicuously absent
analysis.detailed_analysis:
KPI Green Energy is among the fastest-growing listed energy companies in India, and through Fisher's lens, the top-line numbers are genuinely exceptional. Revenue grew from ₹34 Cr in 2019 to ₹1,735 Cr in FY25 — a 93% CAGR — while net profit compounded at 82% to reach ₹325 Cr. Critically, this isn't margin compression growth: operating margins expanded to 30.6% and EBITDA margins held firm at ~33%, suggesting management is not sacrificing profitability for volume. The P/E of 20.6x against 80%+ earnings growth is the kind of mispricing Fisher spent his career hunting — the market is treating this like a mature utility when it is behaving like a high-growth compounder.

The Fisher concern is the structural capital intensity. My scuttlebutt method tells me that independent power producers in India require enormous upfront capital with long payback periods, and KPI is no exception — ₹1,505 Cr capex in FY25 against ₹208 Cr operating cash flow means every rupee of growth must be financed externally. Borrowings have grown to ₹2,533 Cr, D/E at 0.88 is above my comfort threshold of 0.5, and there is no proprietary technology moat to justify a premium over well-capitalized peers like Adani Green or Greenko. Still, India's renewable energy TAM is vast, the company's Surat-based management has demonstrated consistent execution, and the valuation leaves enough room for error to warrant a measured position.
